metas.name: -ec town names
metas.note: Town names ending with “-ec” are common to see in the northern parts of central Croatia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Austrian bollards
metas.note: The island Dugi otok has lots of austrian bollards along the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Beige brick walls
metas.note:
Houses and walls made of beige brick are common on the Adriatic coast. They often feature green shutters.

NOTE: Similar architecture can also be found in some regions in Italy. Additionally, Croatian shutters can also be white, beige etc.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Blue traffic lights
metas.note: Traffic lights in Rijeka are held up by long blue poles that extend out over the road. These are exclusive to the city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Brod Posavina hills
metas.note: Brod Posavina and a small part of east Sisak-Moslavina is very flat and you can often see a ridge of big hills towards the north and south, sometimes the southern hills cannot be seen because of trees. The hills may also not always be directly south or north, some are a bit towards the east or west.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Cracked pavement
metas.note:
Cracked pavement is really common in Sisak-Moslavina and to a lesser extend in Karlovac County but still common.

NOTE: Cracked pavement can ofc be found elsewhere in Croatia but these 2 regions just have the most.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Cres and Dugi otok landscape
metas.note:
Cres and Dugi otok often feature grey/white stone walls along the road and next to it. You will also often see broken rock walls and piles of rocks laying around randomly. This is more common to see in Cres + Cres has more coverage.

These islands also mostly have gen 3 coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatian and Italian street name signs
metas.note: Bilingual street name signs with Croatian and Italian are typically found in Istria, especially in the western cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Cypress trees
metas.note: These tall cypress trees are commonly found near the southern tip of Croatia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Distinct mountain ridge
metas.note: You can see this distinct big white rocky mountain ridge to the north/north-east from Kaštel Stari to Gradac. The ridge looks a bit different depending where you are but it will always be a big white rocky mountain ridge sticking out.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Dubrovnik medieval walls
metas.note: The city of Dubrovnik in the far south of coastal Croatia is famous for its beautifully preserved medieval city walls, which can be seen from many points in and around the Old Town.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Dubrovnik towers
metas.note: You can see these 2 towers on 2 hills in and around Dubrovnik. Sometimes you can see only 1 of the towers.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Exposed rock
metas.note: Exposed rock is very common to see in mainland Primorje-Gorski Kotar and western Karlovac.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Flat landscape
metas.note: The north-eastern region of Croatia is mostly flat and features a lot of agriculture. It is similar in terms of landscape to Hungary and north-western Serbia. Hills/mountains to the south can often be seen in the west and central regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Flat with a mountain ridge
metas.note: The region northeast of Zadar is recognizable as it is flat with a mountain ridge visible in the distance north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Flat with lush green mountains and hills
metas.note:
Lika-Senj and northern Zadar provinces have flat landscapes often with random patches of trees or single trees surrounded by lush green mountains and hills, the eastern part can be a bit more hillier in terms of flatness.

NOTE: South-eastern Croatia has similar landscape but often have rocky mountains instead of lush green mountains. Also this kind of landscape can rarely appear in northern neighboring provinces aswell.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Hilly + agricultural landscape
metas.note: The region north and west of Zagreb is hilly and agricultural.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Ivanšćica and Medvednica
metas.note:
You can often see 2 mountains in the distance towards the south and south east in Varazdin, Krapina-Zagorje and northern Zagreb County.

Ivanšćica (south of Ivanec) is directly seen south, is alot more hillier with big elevation on the surface and has a small tower on top of it on the left side.

Medvednica (north of Zagreb) is towards the south-east, has a way flatter surface than Ivanšćica and has a bigger tower on top of it more towards the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Krk island
metas.note:
Krk island has ALOT of nice looking stone walls with stone pillar walls and fences in between them. Gardens often have lots of different kind of plants and trees in them and you can also sometimes see mountains in the distance.

The town Baška and north of it has these 2 big mountain ridges to the east and west which is very distinct.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Krk island landscape
metas.note: The landscape in Krk is a little hilly, very green, sunny, and has this sandy/rocky white soil next to the road which you often see which is the main part that makes this island distinct. Rock walls are sometimes seen along the road aswell as mountains in the distance. The island will only have gen 4 coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Lots of vineyards
metas.note: There are a lot of vineyards around the town of Ilok, near the Serbian border, west of Novi Sad. You can find vineyards in other parts of Croatia as well, but they are most common in this area. If you see lots of vineyards in a northeastern Croatian landscape, you are more often than not near Ilok.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Makarska mountain ridge
metas.note: Makarska has this ginormous distinct mountain ridge to the north, left side is more rocky and the right side has alot of small trees on it. Smaller towns nearby like Baška Voda and Podgora have a similar mountain ridge.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Medvednica
metas.note: You can often see this big mountain ridge called Medvednica in City of Zagreb County and southern regions of Zagreb County. A tower on the mountain can be seen and sometimes you see tall buildings beneath it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Pag island
metas.note: Pag island is very rocky and dry with a distinct mountain ridge to the north-east. This sugar cane-like plant is also common on the southern half of the island and is I think really unique. Another great meta is that there is a white follow car with a red roof behind the google car, this car is seen from Rtina to Šimuni on the 106.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Park Prirode Žumberak
metas.note: Park Prirode Žumberak is hilly and very forested, but the main thing that makes it recognizable is the large amount of brown leaves that lay on the ground along the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Petrinja
metas.note: The town of Petrinja was severely damaged by an earthquake in 2020. As a result, many buildings can be seen ruined and undergoing repair.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Požega valley
metas.note:
This valley north of Požega can be recognized by the flat and agriculture landscape with hills surrounding you from every side. The hills towards the north are the biggest.

NOTE: The hills towards the east are very small and may not always be fully visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Red numbers
metas.note: Red numbers on electricity poles are most commonly found in Bjelovar-Bilogora province, especially around the city Bjelovar. Their less common in Sisak-Moslavina (most of them are around the town Popovača) and can very rarely appear in nearby provinces.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Red soil
metas.note: The north-western region of Istria, south of the Italian city of Trieste, sometimes has distinct red soil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Rijeka mountains
metas.note: You can often see these big mountains to the west in and around the city Rijeka.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Rocky mountains
metas.note: The Adriatic coast features rocky mountains similar to those seen in Montenegro or Albania. Shrubs are more common instead of trees along the coast, especially in the south. This coastal region has a lot of islands and peninsulas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Split
metas.note: Split, the 2nd biggest city in Croatia, is a distinct city surrounded by water, with big mountain ridges to the north and east. It has lots of big apartment buildings and 1 sky scraper which can sometimes be seen. An island can also sometimes be seen towards the west.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Trams
metas.note:
Zagreb and Osijek are the only two cities in Croatia with trams.

Tips: Zagreb uses blue trams and busses, Osijek does not. Zagreb has a big mountain in the north, Osijek does not. Zagreb has unique street signs everywhere, Osijek does not. Zagreb in general looks alot different, its more developed with taller buildings and is hilly on some parts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Zagreb
metas.note:
Croatia’s capital Zagreb has a distinct big city feel. Apartment blocks can be seen throughout the city. The northern part of the city is hilly. Furthermore, Zagreb has blue electric trams and busses, it has a big mountain to the north, and has unique street name signs.

NOTE: In addition to regular car coverage, Zagreb also has various urban sidewalk trekkers, often made with a Generation 2 camera.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/croatia.

metas.name: Zagreb street name signs
metas.note: These 2 dark blue street signs are unique to Zagreb. It always has a white line next to the street name.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.
